name: Conditions for practice in the Haṭhapradīpikā

definitions.definition: The text names a fitting place (1.12-13), setting aside all worries and practising under the guru's path (1.14), six things that destroy and six that further yoga (1.15-16), secrecy (1.11), the pursuit of practice not talk or dress (1.65-66), and open eligibility for anyone who practises (1.64).

name: The six that further yoga (HYP 1.16)

definitions.definition: Enthusiasm (utsāha), bold resolve (sāhasa), steadiness (dhairya), knowledge of the truth (tattvajñāna), firm conviction (niścaya) and giving up the company of people (janasaṅgaparityāga).

definitions.definition: The text says haṭha is to be kept secret, potent when hidden and impotent when disclosed (1.11); the six acts are to be kept secret (2.23); the ten mudrās are to be guarded like a casket of jewels and told to no one (3.9); mahāmudrā is 'not to be given to just anyone' (3.18).

name: Mind and breath move together (HYP)

definitions.definition: The text says the mind moves when the breath moves and is still when it is still (2.2); by whom the breath is bound, the mind is bound, and conversely (4.21); the mind has two causes, latent impression and breath (4.22); each dissolves where the other dissolves (4.23); they are like milk and water (4.24); their dissolution together is the state of liberation (4.25); mind, breath, bindu and body are steady in that order (4.28).

name: Contemplations that dissolve the mind (HYP 4.50-62)

definitions.definition: Making the mind supportless and thinking of nothing (4.50, 4.55, 4.57); void and full within and without like a pot in space (4.56); the world as a construct of resolve (saṅkalpa) (4.58); mind dissolving in reality as camphor in fire (4.59); knowing and the known destroyed together (4.60); duality not perceived when the mind is unmanī (4.61); kaivalya remaining when the mind has dissolved (4.62).

name: Practice, not talk, dress or scripture-reading

definitions.definition: The text says accomplishment does not come from reading the scriptures alone (1.65), nor from wearing a garb or talking about it (1.66); some are deluded by scriptures and reasoning and do not know the tāraka, 'that which carries across' (4.40); talk of knowledge without the corresponding state is boasting and false prattle (4.114).

name: Warnings of the text on breath practice

definitions.definition: The text's own cautions: the breath is tamed only slowly as a lion or elephant, 'anyathā hanti sādhakam' (2.15); wrong practice gives rise to all disease (2.16), naming hiccup, breathlessness, cough and pains of head, ears and eyes (2.17); release only 'śanaireva na vegataḥ' (2.9) and 'śanaiḥ śanaireva recayennaiva vegataḥ' (3.13); holding only 'yathāśakti', as far as one is able (2.7, 3.21); only in proper measure (2.18); with the guru's path (2.1); the first practice small, 'svalpaṃ prathamasādhanam' (3.31); 'alpāhāro yadi bhavedagnirdahati tatkṣaṇāt' in the inverted practice (3.81).

definitions.definition: The final verse of the text says that until the breath enters the middle path, bindu is firm and reality arises like the natural state in meditation, talk of knowledge is 'dambhamithyāpralāpaḥ'.

name: Marks of the yogin joined in samādhi (HYP 4.106-113)

definitions.definition: The text states that the yogin in samādhi hears no conch or drum and his body is like wood (4.106), stays as if dead and is liberated (4.107), is not eaten by Time nor bound by karma (4.108), knows no smell, taste, form, touch or sound (4.109), whose mind is neither asleep nor awake (4.110), who knows no cold, heat, pain or pleasure (4.111), stays as if asleep in waking without breath-movement (4.112), and cannot be slain by weapons or seized by mantras (4.113).

name: The four states of the yoga of inner sound (ārambha, ghaṭa, paricaya, niṣpatti)

definitions.definition: The text says all yogas have a fourfold state: beginning (4.69). In ārambha the knot of Brahmā is pierced and bliss and tinkling sounds arise (4.70-71); in ghaṭa the breath goes in the middle and the knot of Viṣṇu is pierced (4.72-73); in paricaya the mardala sound and the great void (4.74-75); in niṣpatti the knot of Rudra is pierced and the mind becomes one, called rājayoga (4.76-77).

name: Haṭha and rājayoga depend on each other

definitions.definition: Haṭha is taught solely for rājayoga (1.2); its practices run up to rājayoga's fruit (1.67); without haṭha rājayoga does not succeed, and the reverse (2.76); mudrās do not shine without rājayoga (3.126); those who know only haṭha are said to lack the fruit of their toil (4.79); all haṭha and laya methods are for rājayoga (4.103); the seed, field, water image (4.104).
